metadata.title: HOOD, COIN Get Wedbush Outperform Ratings: Here’s What The Firm Sees In Fintech’s Next Growth Phase

content.text:
-
Wedbush starts coverage of Robinhood with an 'Outperform' rating and a price target of $80.
-
Block and Circle received a 'Neutral' rating.
-
According to Wedbush, fintech growth drivers are shifting from transaction-based fees to higher-value services.
The next phase of fintech growth may depend on how many payments companies process and more on the services they can sell around those transactions. Wedbush initiated coverage of Robinhood Markets (HOOD), Coinbase Global (COIN), Circle (CRCL) and Block (XYZ), with the firm favoring HOOD and COIN as transaction-based revenue continues to face pressure.
In a research note to clients on Tuesday, Wedbush analyst Moshe Katri gave Robinhood and Coinbase 'Outperform' ratings, according to TheFly. The firm assigned 'Neutral' ratings to Circle and Block.
Katri, the Managing Director in the Disruptive Technology, Media, & Sports Investment Banking group at Wedbush Securities believes that fintech companies will increasingly have to look beyond the fees they collect on individual payments to find the next source of growth.
Wedbush's Ratings and Price Targets For Fintech Stocks
Moving Beyond Payment Fees
"The bigger driver now is the pivot away from per-transaction fees, which keep compressing," Katri said.
In his research note, Katri highlighted the industry's shift away from per-transaction fees, which continue to face pricing pressure, toward higher-value offerings such as cybersecurity, fraud prevention, data, rewards, and identity tools.
HOOD, COIN Retail Sentiment Remains Bearish
The company set a price target of $80 for Robinhood stock, which implies a 23% upside from Tuesday's close of $65.
HOOD stock was down over 1% in overnight trading after closing 2% lower on Tuesday's session. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around HOOD remained in the 'bearish' zone, accompanied by 'low' chatter levels over the past day.
Wedbush also set a price target of $127 for Coinbase, which implies a 25% upside from the stock's previous close of $102.
COIN stock extended its slide in overnight trading after closing over 5% lower on Tuesday. On Stocktwits retail sentiment around COIN remained in the 'bearish' zone, with chatter levels at normal over the past day.
Circle, Block Rated Neutral
Wedbush was a bit more reserved about the other two names in crypto stocks. It set a $55 target for Circle, the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, which would be a 17% upside from its last close of $47.
